labels.expected_answer: Neither park allows ordinary pets on all hiking trails. In Yosemite, pets can use developed areas and fully paved roads, sidewalks, and bicycle paths unless signed otherwise; listed examples include Bridalveil Fall, Lower Yosemite Fall, the paved Cook’s Meadow path including boardwalks, and the paved road to Mirror Lake, but not its unpaved loop. The general trail ban includes Vernal Fall even when the pet is carried; Wawona Meadow Loop is an exception. Other listed routes are Chowchilla Mountain Road, Four Mile and Eleven Mile fire roads (not Yosemite Valley’s Four Mile Trail), Carlon Road to Hodgdon Meadow (not Carlon Falls), Old Big Oak Flat Road from Hodgdon Meadow to Tuolumne Grove parking lot (not the trail), and the road within Tuolumne Grove (not its nature trail). Unplowed snow-covered roads, wilderness, and undeveloped areas are prohibited. Yosemite requires a leash no longer than six feet or other physical restraint, and leashed pets cannot be unattended; walk-in and group campsites, including Camp 4, exclude pets. On Grand Canyon’s South Rim, leashed pets can walk trails above the rim and developed areas, including Mather and Desert View campgrounds and Trailer Village. Pets must stay on a leash up to six feet at all times, and cannot go below the rim or ride park shuttles. Trained service animals have separate rules; these ordinary-pet permissions do not make a companion dog a service dog.
